messages:
derek_sales: Quick heads-up — prospective enterprise (FinServ) scoping a hybrid deal. They want 300K reserved tokens/day for 12 months + flexible overage credits and an option to convert unused reserved to credits quarterly. Asking for a blended per-token commitment rate + capped overage price. Can product advise on standard policy + risks? TL;DR: need packaging guidance and launch criteria.

maria_pm: Thanks. Do we have their expected QPS/seq length? Also they want per-model pricing or single flat rate across models?

derek_sales: Mostly chat usage, avg seq ~150 tokens, spikes to 800 daily. They want flat rate across our LLM catalog to keep procurement simple.

ashwin_eng: Flat across models is risky — perf/cost varies drastically. If they're committed to a single SKU we should define allowed model tiers (gpt-tier, open-large, quantized) and fallback rules. Reserved tokens need to map to capacity (GPU hours). We need peak concurrency to ensure latency SLOs.

rachel_support: FYI ran a similar request for RetailCo last Q — we allowed quarterly roll-forward of up to 20% unused commit to credits, capped at 3 months, with overage at 1.5x commit unit price. Sales okayed it. Blockers: ambiguous burst policy caused a latency SLO miss.

maria_pm: Proposal: standard hybrid packaging = (1) commit contract with reserved capacity (GPU pool) tied to token bucket; (2) quarterly roll-forward up to 25% unused -> credits; (3) overage price = 1.6x commit per-token; (4) explicit model tier whitelist; (5) SLA/latency tiers documented. Need RevOps + Legal to pre-approve template. Thoughts?

ashwin_eng: Agree but suggest technical guardrail: bursts over sustained 2x baseline for >10min auto-throttle and route to higher-cost fallback model. Also require a usage profile appendix for capacity planning.

derek_sales: Good. Customer will push back on 1.6x. They want 1.2x capped. Any business flexibility?

maria_pm: Negotiable if commit size or term increases. We can trade rate for longer term or higher commit. Launch criteria: RevOps approved pricing sheet, contract addendum template, billing automation mapping, and capacity baseline accepted by infra. If any missing -> escalate to pricing committee.

rachel_support: Add test plan: customers must pass a smoke run on our staging to validate latency at expected concurrency before go-live.

billing-bot: Generated sample calculation for proposed package:
```
commit_tokens_per_month = 300000 * 30
commit_unit_price = $0.0008 per token
monthly_commit_charge = commit_tokens_per_month * commit_unit_price
overage_unit_price = commit_unit_price * 1.6
overage_charge = max(0, actual_usage - commit_tokens_per_month) * overage_unit_price
```
Send to revops@ for approval.

maria_pm: Next steps: Derek, share usage appendix + procurement timeline. I'll draft a pricing sheet and get RevOps on a 1:1 today. If customer insists on 1.2x, we'll prepare a counter-offer requiring min term/commit increase.

derek_sales: On it — sending details now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
